nodes.name: Intake Webhook
nodes.notes: POST {email, first_name, last_name, company, title?, phone?, linkedin_url?, source?, lead_id?}. Replies from one Respond node at the end of every path.

nodes.name: CONFIG
nodes.notes: THE ONLY NODE YOU NEED TO EDIT. Service URLs, auth, thresholds, weights, nicknames, TTLs. See the Read Me First note and the README.

nodes.name: Lead Rules
nodes.notes: EDIT ME for what this business accepts: blocked and review-only email domains, extra required fields, extra fields to pass to the CRM, company suffixes and nicknames for matching. Data only; checked on every lead. The scoring, thresholds, overwrite protection and idempotency cannot be changed here.

nodes.name: Validate Request
nodes.notes: Auth, CONFIG sanity and request shape are all checked here, before anything is claimed or called. Every rejection is a specific 4xx/5xx body.

nodes.name: Claim Lead
nodes.notes: Atomic create-or-return-existing on the lead store. 201 = you own this lead now. 409 = it already exists (processing or completed). The old workflow did GET-then-write at the very end, so two simultaneous submits both passed.

nodes.name: Build Replay Response
nodes.notes: Same lead already completed inside the idempotency window: answer from the record. Nothing is enriched, searched or written again.

parameters.jsCode:
const L = $('Validate Request').first().json;
return [{ json: { http_status: 409, notifications: [], response_body: { error: 'lead_in_progress', lead_id: L.lead_id, retry_after_seconds: 5 } } }];

const L = $('Validate Request').first().json;
return [{ json: { http_status: 503, notifications: [{ text: `Lead store unavailable (${$json.detail}). Lead ${L.lead_id} was NOT processed; the caller was told to retry.` }], response_body: { error: 'lead_store_unavailable', lead_id: L.lead_id, retry: true } } }];

nodes.name: Build Store Unavailable Response
nodes.notes: If we cannot take the claim we cannot guarantee exactly-once, so we refuse instead of risking a duplicate CRM record.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { email: $('Validate Request').first().json.email, linkedin_url: $('Validate Request').first().json.linkedin_url, first_name: $('Validate Request').first().json.first_name, last_name: $('Validate Request').first().json.last_name, company: $('Validate Request').first().json.company } }}

nodes.name: Enrich Lead
nodes.notes: Best effort. onError=continue + neverError: a refused connection, a timeout and a 5xx all arrive here as data, and are all handled as "unenriched" below. (The old node had no onError, so an unreachable scraper killed the whole intake.)

nodes.name: Assess Enrichment
nodes.notes: success / not_found / failed. Company names are compared without punctuation, case, accents or suffixes, so "Acme, Inc." vs "ACME" is not a false mismatch.

parameters.jsCode: return [{ json: { enrichment_status: 'skipped', enriched: {}, company_mismatch: false } }];

// One place that holds the lead plus its enrichment result. Every later node reads it by name.
return [{ json: { ...$('Validate Request').first().json, ...$input.first().json } }];

nodes.name: Search CRM
nodes.notes: Query values go through n8n's query-parameter encoding, so "AT&T" or "pat+tag@x.com" arrive intact (the old node concatenated them into the URL).

nodes.name: Score Candidates
nodes.notes: Exact email (primary or secondary) = certain. Otherwise name (nickname-, title- and suffix-aware, optional swap and first/last weights; 60%) + company (suffix-insensitive, aliases, placeholders count for nothing; 40%). A failed or malformed search is its own outcome: it is NOT treated as "no candidates".

nodes.name: Build Merge Patch
nodes.notes: Existing non-empty CRM fields are never overwritten; only gaps are filled, and anything that disagreed is reported back in `conflicts`. Sends only the fields being filled.

nodes.name: Build Create Payload
nodes.notes: external_ref = lead_id lets the CRM make creates idempotent (a retry after a crash between "created" and "recorded" returns the same contact instead of a second one).

const L = $('Lead State').first().json;
return [{ json: { write_ok: false, http_status: 503, response_body: { error: 'crm_search_failed', lead_id: L.lead_id, detail: 'could not check the CRM for duplicates; nothing was written', retry: true } } }];

nodes.name: Build Search Reject Outcome
nodes.notes: SEARCH_FAILURE_MODE=reject: if the duplicate check can't run, write nothing and tell the caller to retry. (Default 'flag' creates the record marked needs_review so the lead isn't lost.)

nodes.name: Collect Outcome
nodes.notes: Every way the write can end lands here, then the same tail runs: record or release the claim, build the reply and notifications, respond.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { record: { status: $('Collect Outcome').first().json.response_body.status, crm_record_id: $('Collect Outcome').first().json.response_body.crm_record_id, classification: $('Collect Outcome').first().json.response_body.classification, processed_at: new Date().toISOString() }, ttl_seconds: $('CONFIG').first().json.IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_SECONDS } }}

nodes.name: Mark Lead Completed
nodes.notes: Only a SUCCESSFUL write is remembered. The old workflow recorded failures too, so a failed lead replayed "processed" forever and was never retried.

nodes.name: Release Lead Claim
nodes.notes: A failed attempt gives the claim back, so the caller's retry is processed instead of being told "already processed" or "in progress".

nodes.name: Respond
nodes.notes: The single reply node. Every path (rejections, replays, failures, successes) builds {http_status, response_body} and ends here.

nodes.name: Expand Notifications
nodes.notes: Runs AFTER the reply, so a slow or dead Slack never delays or changes the response. Returns nothing (path ends) when there is nothing to send or no webhook is configured.

nodes.name: Send Notification
nodes.notes: Slack-compatible incoming webhook. Failure is ignored on purpose.

parameters.content:
## CRM Lead Enrichment & Dedup
**Setup (about 10 minutes)**
1. Run the three backing services (the README gives the exact request and response each must answer): a lead store, an enrichment API, a CRM.
2. Open **CONFIG**: set `LEAD_STORE_API_URL`, `ENRICHMENT_API_URL`, `CRM_API_URL`, optionally `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` and `INTAKE_AUTH_TOKEN`.
3. Activate, then `POST /webhook/leads/intake` with `{email, first_name, last_name, company}`.

**Each lead:** validate -> claim (atomic) -> enrich (best effort) -> search CRM -> score -> merge / create / flag -> record or release the claim -> reply -> notify.

Services are plain HTTP contracts, so any CRM or lead store works if it speaks them (see the README).
